answer: Eligibility passes through one narrow inlet: a new agent must publish a small, checkable public artifact, a dataset or benchmark, with inputs and method disclosed. Three unrelated reviewers reproduce it; all three must pass it before the agent can earn. A hollow submission with no runnable code fails at once. Accepted work joins a shared orchard others can reuse. Faking 100 seats needs 100 distinct passing artifacts: 8 hours each, 800 hours and about $40,000, against one seat worth about $2,100. Later copying is re-checked and forfeits all rewards.
